entries.proposition: The study is one cross-sectional, population-based sample of 801 unrelated Spanish Caucasian adults; this is a quantitative-trait association study in the general population, not a patient or loss-of-function cohort.
entries.snippet: This study comprises 801 non related Caucasian men (n = 433, 54.05%) and women (n = 368, 45.95%) who were recruited by a simple random sampling approach from a cross-sectional population-based epidemiological survey in Spain

entries.proposition: The analysed variants were 1045 common SNPs, 894 of them imputed from HapMap CEU rather than genotyped.
entries.snippet: Finally, 1045 SNPs (151 directly genotyped and 894 imputed, all of them with MAF ≥ 0.10) were analysed for association with HDL, TGs and HDL/TG ratio using the linear regression procedure included in the PLINK software

entries.proposition: The authors applied no multiple-comparison correction and set the significance threshold at nominal p below 0.05.
entries.snippet: We have not applied multiple comparison correction because we consider it over-conservative for the replication of a previously described gene specially given that most genotypes analysed in this report are derived from a small number of observed genotypes; a p value under 0.05 is interpreted as significant.

entries.proposition: The strongest HDL signal in the study is intron-8 rs2047927 at p = 0.003, with a negative beta (lower HDL per allele), in a different LD block from the rs4888865/rs4145518 signals, whose betas are positive.
entries.snippet: The strongest associations in the region were observed for the rs4888865 (p = 0.006, β = 0.96) and the rs4145518 (p = 0.007, β = 1.03) polymorphisms.

entries.proposition: Region 3, the second intron-8 HDL region, has its best SNP rs2047927 at p = 0.003 with beta -2.25.
entries.snippet: of which the rs2047927 showed the highest significance (p = 0.003, β = -2.25)

entries.proposition: The largest triglyceride signal is at the 5' end of WWOX (promoter to intron 4), rs11645006, p = 0.0002, beta -13.81 (lower TG per allele).
entries.snippet: a broad region that extends from the promoter to the 4th intron, with the largest association at rs11645006 (p = 0.0002, β = -13.81).

entries.proposition: No intron-8 region is associated with HDL in the haplotype analysis, so the HDL signal that anchors the WWOX-HDL literature is not carried by a haplotype block here.
entries.snippet: Moreover, none of the intron 8 regions are associated with HDL in the haplotypic analysis, although region 2 shows a trend for association (p = 0.07).

entries.proposition: Global haplotype test for region 1 (promoter to intron 4): TG p = 0.003, HDL p = 0.018, TG/HDL p = 0.006.
entries.snippet: GLOBAL HAPLOTYPIC EFFECT F = 3.13p = 0.003 F = 2.435p = 0.018 F = 2.836p = 0.006

entries.proposition: The study did not replicate the originally reported HDL variant rs2548861, and the authors give three reasons the failure could be technical or power-related.
entries.snippet: In our study, we failed to replicate the association of the rs2548861 with HDL.

entries.proposition: The authors state their study is underpowered below an effect size of 0.14.
entries.snippet: We estimate that our study is underpowered for SNPs with effect sizes below 0.14, so we can not rule out power issues.

entries.proposition: The authors themselves state that some associations may be chance and that independent replication is needed.
entries.snippet: We cannot rule out that some of the observed associations could have arisen by chance, reason why additional, independent replications are needed.

entries.proposition: The introduction records, citing the 2008 knockout-mouse paper, that Wwox-null mice are hypotriglyceridemic and hypocholesterolemic: the direction of the mouse null is stated beside the human association.
entries.snippet: In fact, WWOX knockout mouse model exhibits hypotriglyceridemia and hypocholesterolemia among other metabolic disturbances [26].

entries.proposition: The paper's functional step is a suggestion only: it speculates that variation in the 5' region could modify WWOX expression and states that functional analyses are needed.
entries.snippet: It is tempting to speculate that genetic variations in this region could modify the expression of the WWOX gene. Functional analyses are needed to answer this hypothesis.

entries.proposition: PANEL READING, Figure 1 (Manhattan-style plots of -log10 P along WWOX, three traits). In 1A (HDL) the highest points reach about 2.5-2.6 within shaded region 3; in 1B (TG) the highest points reach about 3.6 within shaded region 1; in 1C (TG/HDL) about 3.0 in region 2 and 2.7 in region 1. No point in any panel reaches the 4.0 axis top. All points are drawn as one series (Chr16) with no marker distinguishing genotyped from imputed SNPs.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 1A y-axis -log10(P) 0 to 4.0 with a horizontal blue line at 1.3; shaded zones 2 and 3 carry the highest points (about 2.5); Fig 1B shaded zone 1 carries points up to about 3.6; Fig 1C zones 1 and 2; legend box reads Chr16 only.
